PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:02 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:00 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items: 

Items #1- Staff made a presentation, City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on this item.  

Item #2- two matters were discussed - one matter was before the regular city Council and another after the regular city Council meeting.  Staff made a presentation, and no reportable action was taken on this items. 

Item #3- staff made a presentation, City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on this item.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called regular meeting to order at 6:02 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Transportation Director McFerguson led the Pledge of Allegiance

INVOCATION Mayor Altamirano offered the invocation

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. City Videos

PUBLIC COMMENT Union President Franklin Aroyo requested that the City Council consider declaring the City of Commerce a Sanctuary City. Additionally, he urged the reinstatement of the Search and Rescue Team to ensure preparedness for emergencies.

Gloria Nezahualcoyl expressed concerns about the mismanagement of social club funds. She also noted that transportation services have been reduced, requiring activities to conclude by 2:00 PM, which poses an inconvenience for seniors, as the Senior Center remains open until 5:00 PM. In response, Mayor Altamirano directed staff to schedule a meeting with Ms. Nezahualcoyl.

Jason Stinnette presented a letter proposing the establishment of a Commerce Sustainability and Resilience Commission. The commission would focus on energy conservation efforts and be composed of residents, union representatives, and other stakeholders. Mayor Altamirano requested a meeting with the representatives to discuss the proposal further.

Planning Commissioner Ernesto Gonzalez supported the need for a sustainability commission, emphasizing the importance of preparing for and adapting to a changing climate.




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Councilmember Garcia requested to pull Item #4 for discussion. She inquired about the lifespan of rotary compressors, to which Director McFerguson responded that they typically last 10–12 years and receive proper maintenance. Councilmember Garcia then asked about the cost for two compressors, and Director McFerguson stated that the total cost is $50,000.

Councilmember Argumedo moved, seconded by Councilmember Rebollo, to adopt a Resolution approving the purchase of two rotary air screw compressors through the United States General Services Administration (GSA) 

3.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 11A, and 11B

4.. Purchase of Two Rotary Air Screw Compressors Through the United States General Services Administration (GSA)

5.. Transportation’s Operational Report for the First Quarter of Fiscal Year 2025

2.. Approval of Minutes

SCHEDULED MATTERS

6.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE There were no presentation.

7.. Agreement with IBE Digital for IT Remediation Services  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo City Manager Hernandez provided a brief summary of the staff report.

Councilmember Argumedo requested an update on the breach that occurred at the end of last year, specifically asking for the results of the investigation and measures taken to prevent future incidents. City Manager Hernandez stated that the City Council would receive a report on the matter.

A representative from IBE clarified that the current proposal is for the approval of the surveillance system framework. The implementation and management of the system will require additional Council approval at a later date.  



9.. Committee and Commission Appointments Councilmember Garcia re-appointed Kiana Hernandez to the Education Commission and Connie Artega to the Library Commission. 

8.. Consideration of Rejection of Commercial Cannabis Permit Applicant Nos. 18-036 and 18-028  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo City Manager Hernandez provided a brief introduction, followed by Management Analyst Delgado, who gave a detailed overview of the report. 

PUBLIC HEARING

10.. Allocation for the 51st Year of Community Development Grant (CDBG) Funds for Fiscal Year 2025-2026  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Mayor Altamirano opened the Public Hearing. Seeing no one wishing to address the City Council on this item, Mayor Altamirano closed the Public Hearing.

Acting Director of Economic Development and Planning Morales provided an overview of the staff report. Mayor Pro Tem Lainez inquired about the amount spent last year and whether unutilized funds could be carried over. Director Morales explained that CDBG funding is based on population. Mayor Pro Tem Lainez emphasized the importance of fully utilizing the funds and ensuring they directly benefit the community.

Councilmember Argumedo assured that the City spends 100% of the allocated funds each year and recommended exploring additional resources that the City could leverage.

Further discussion took place regarding informing residents about available funds and the types of repairs that could be covered by CDBG monies.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Rebollo wished the community a Happy New Year and expressed gratitude to the Parks and Recreation Department for their outstanding programming, including activities at the Teen Center. Councilmember Rebollo also thanked the City Manager and staff for their swift response during the recent LA fires, including donations of water, partnerships with civic organizations, and transportation assistance to affected areas.

 Councilmember Rebollo acknowledged members of the community stepping up to help, highlighting Makayla Rice, who has been collecting donations in Commerce for fire relief efforts. She noted the urgent need for volunteers to help sort donations and asked the community to keep emergency personnel in their thoughts. Additionally, Councilmember Rebollo recognized Anthony Diaz, who used his tow trucks to assist in Pasadena, and other businesses that helped provide food for emergency responders.

Councilmember Garcia reported attending a local aerobics class, noting its high participation. Councilmember Garcia also attended the Holiday Craft Event, the Children's Holiday Program, and the Holiday Breakfast for seniors.

 Councilmember Garcia requested that the City Manager ensure N95 masks are made available to seniors. City Manager Hernandez confirmed that the masks had arrived and would be distributed the next day. Councilmember Garcia also inquired about emergency preparedness, asking if emergency bins are fully stocked and whether staff is adequately trained. City Manager Hernandez stated that the City’s Hazard Mitigation Plan needs to be updated and will be brought before the Council. Councilmember Garcia further suggested preparing "Go Kits" for residents to use in emergencies.  She extended her condolences to the families of Timothy Griego, Raquel Arriaga, and Elena Cruz.

Councilmember Argumedo wished everyone a Happy New Year and thanked the community and staff for their hard work. He mentioned receiving calls regarding deportation concerns and asked whether the City could explore ways to assist affected residents. He noted that a brochure had been provided by the office of Congresswoman Garcia and suggested the City use it to help direct residents to appropriate resources.

 Councilmember Argumedo also requested that the Council consider bringing back the Commerce Pageant and reiterated his condolences to the Griego and Arriaga families. Additionally, Councilmember Argumedo  reminded residents about the City’s upcoming 65th Birthday Celebration.

Mayor Pro Tem Lainez thanked City staff for their incredible efforts in organizing holiday events. He also acknowledged residents and businesses that stepped up to assist during the LA fires. Mayor Pro Tem Lainez concluded by wishing everyone a prosperous 2025.

Mayor Altamirano wished the community a Happy New Year and asked City Manager Hernandez about the availability of indoor air filters from the South Coast Air Quality Management District (AQMD). He requested that staff explore ways to distribute more filters to residents and assist with the application process.



ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 8:33 p.m. in memory of Tim Griego, Raquel Arriaga, Elicia Carbajal and Elena Cruz.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
